_comment: Hand-maintained. Every dispatch in the Diaries, and the two categories they sit in.
diaries.html is generated from this file by scripts/build-diaries.mjs. Adding a post is
one entry here plus one file in content/ — there is no CMS and no database, deliberately.
THE DIARIES IS ONE PAGE (changed 17 Aug 2026)
It used to be a hub of cards that sent you off to /restaurants and
/article-contemporary-indian-wear. Those two pages are gone: their content is now inline
on /diaries under the category it belongs to, and both old URLs 301 to it. Every post's
href is therefore an ANCHOR on the diaries page, not a page of its own — #annamalai, and
so on — and the ids below are what those anchors are made from. Changing an id changes a
URL that has been shared, so treat them as permanent.
A category with no posts is not rendered at all: an empty section on a page whose
rendered at all: an empty section on a page whose whole job is to show there is something
to read is worse than a shorter page. Order here is order on the page.
Fields on a post:
id       stable slug. IS the on-page anchor and part of a public URL — permanent.
cat      must match a category id below
kind     'article' renders the body as long-form prose with its own headings.
'review' renders it as a review entry with a photo beside the text.
title    the heading, and the name in the structured data
blurb    one or two sentences for the card at the top of the page; keep it short
body     file under content/, holding the post's HTML with no chrome around it
date     ISO. Sorts the page and picks the cards on the homepage strip
photo    key into images/derived/manifest.json, or null for a spice-gradient panel
kicker   the small line above the title on a card. Usually the place or the dish
verdict  reviews only: { label, tone } where tone is real | mild | trap
meta     reviews only: the district · cuisine · format line
order    reviews only: what to actually order
reading  articles only: minutes, shown in the byline
cuisine  reviews only: fed to the Review structured data as the restaurant's cuisine
region   reviews only: the Prague district, for the same

categories.name: What I wear
categories.note: Contemporary Indian wear, and how it actually works in a European city.

categories.name: Food I love in the city
categories.note: Every Indian place in Prague, judged honestly — plus the fully vegan spots worth the tram ride.
categories.disclosure: No paid collaborations or review invites, just my experiences. I compare the food in the city to what I have grown up eating :)

categories.name: Mindfulness
categories.note: Practice, stillness, and what Indian spiritual traditions look like from a European weekday.

posts.title: Contemporary Indian wear on the streets of Prague
posts.blurb: Not Goa-hippie, not festival sari. The new age of Indian wear — earthy palettes, hand-loomed craft, avant-garde fusion — and exactly how to style it into a European wardrobe.

posts.title: Annamalai
posts.blurb: Cooked to order in a dim underground room in Nové Město, with the TV blaring Indian songs. Tastes vary day to day, the way fresh cooking does. The only South Indian I keep going back to.

posts.title: INDelicious Bistro
posts.blurb: North and South Indian street food in Nusle. Super tasty, and somehow never leaves you bloated — which is the whole trick with street food.
posts.meta: Nusle · North/South Indian · quick bites and full meals
posts.order: pav bhaji, spinach paneer paratha, vada pav, bhel.

posts.title: Dosa Dosa
posts.blurb: Fully vegan South Indian on Újezd, and a perfect breakfast stop. California dosa, masala dosa, uttapam, buckwheat noodles.

posts.title: Pastva
posts.blurb: A rotating fully vegan menu in Anděl, and staff who clearly enjoy feeding people. Burgers, risotto, dumplings, borscht, hummus, croquettes.
posts.order: whatever is on the rotating menu.

posts.title: Palo Verde Bistro
posts.blurb: Mushroom lamps, cosmic skies, and a spinach chimney worth going back for. Fully vegan, on Žitná.

posts.title: Hello world
posts.blurb: The first note in a new category — why mindfulness gets its own shelf here, and what will land in it.
